headline: Burn pECX from BitWindow — the window closes at the betanet fork.
message: The Alphanet ends at Bitcoin block 967,680 (expected Saturday 19 September, ~08:00 UTC). Burn in BitWindow before then: the Receive page carries a Burn Transaction card that sends your pECX to the Bitcoin eater address and puts your wallet's own first address in the OP_RETURN. That address receives 1/100 of what you burn as real ECX at mainnet, rounded up — 1,013 pECX becomes 10.134 ECX. A burn that does not make it into an Alphanet block before the fork is never credited, so the practical deadline is a block, not a date.

expect.note: Balances do not carry over from alpha to beta: the betanet is a separate chain that forks Bitcoin at 967,680. Details: /betanet/.

spec.network: pECX on the ECX Alphanet — the burn card only exists on Alphanet
spec.ratio: 1/100 of what you burn, rounded up to a whole ECX satoshi: 1,000 → 10 ECX, 1,013 → 10.13 ECX
spec.minimum: Strictly more than 1,000 pECX. Exactly 1,000 is rejected.
spec.deadline: Before the betanet fork — BTC block 967,680, expected Saturday 19 September 2026 at about 08:00 UTC. BitWindow stops offering the card when the Alphanet stops.
spec.mainnet: ECX mainnet at BTC block ~973,728, on or around 31 October 2026. The betanet forked earlier, at block 967,680 on 19 September — that fork is on the betanet page, not this one.
spec.payout: The OP_RETURN carries the wallet's own first address, and the ECX credit lands there. BitWindow fills it in — you do not type an address.
spec.source_note: Verified against the implementation, not a document: ECXBurnAddress, ECXBurnMinimumSats = 100,000,000,000 sat and ECXCreditSats = ceil(burn/100) in sidechain-orchestrator/wallet/ecx_burn.go. No official specification exists.

guide.title: Update BitWindow, and be on Alphanet
guide.detail: The burn is new, so an older build does not have it — update from inside the app (LayerTwo ships through Sparkle, not GitHub releases). The card only exists on Alphanet; on any other network it is not shown at all.

guide.title: Go to Wallet → Receive, with an Electrum wallet selected and unlocked
guide.detail: It must be a wallet holding its own private key: BitWindow refuses Core wallets, watch-only wallets and hardware wallets — "This wallet cannot sign this burn. Select a software wallet with its private key." The Burn Transaction card sits below the receive QR.

guide.title: Enter the amount, read the two panels, press Burn Transaction
guide.detail: Up to 8 decimals, and it must exceed 1,000. BitWindow then shows Alphanet → Real ECX (what you give up, what you get) and the outputs: your amount to the eater address, plus a 0-value OP_RETURN carrying your wallet's first address. Press Burn Transaction, and keep the txid it returns — that is your proof of burn.

spec.deadline_short: before the betanet fork, BTC 967,680, ~19 Sep 08:00 UTC

warnings: It cannot be undone. The eater address has no private key, by design — those pECX are gone, and what comes back is the credit at mainnet, nothing else.
1,000 is not enough. The threshold is exclusive: burning exactly 1,000 gets you nothing, and there is no topping up afterwards.

Your ECX is credited to your wallet's first address — you never type a payout address. If you cannot sign for that address later, you cannot reach the ECX, so do not burn from a wallet you are about to throw away.
The clock is Bitcoin's, not yours. A burn left in the Alphanet mempool when the last alpha block is mined is never credited.
This came out of the project's own Telegram group; there is still no official specification document. Ask before moving anything you would miss.
Nobody legitimate needs your seed phrase or private key to help you redeem. Anyone who asks is robbing you.
